notes (all non-blocking, with file:line):
- `packages/runtime/src/cli/hook.ts:158`: `VCS_REMINDER` forbids `--amend` and bypassing hooks "without the user's approval". `root/version-control.md:14-15` says "unless the user asks" and allows amending your own unpushed commit. Confirmed by reading. Align the wording; the reminder wins at runtime.
- `packages/runtime/src/setup/doctor.ts:75-87`: doctor destructures only `{ file }`, so the `notice` about a rejected git top-level is dropped. It uses the same fallback file as setup, so only the message is missing.
- `packages/runtime/src/setup/settings.ts:107-114`: the settings write comes before `addRecorded`. If the record write fails, the added keys are never recorded and `--undo` keeps them as "unrecorded". The window is narrow. Writing the record first would instead risk removing a user's own equal value.
- `packages/runtime/src/setup/record.ts:63-89`: load, modify and save of the shared record is not atomic across processes. Records for different files coexist correctly in one process; only simultaneous setups can lose an entry.
- `packages/runtime/src/setup/record.ts:28`: record keys are `resolve(file)`. A path reached through a symlink or with different drive-letter casing on Windows gets no match, and undo then keeps everything. The failure is safe (nothing is wrongly removed), and the unrecorded `~` line tells the user to remove it by hand.
- `packages/runtime/src/setup/settings.ts:236`: `clearRecorded` drops the whole file record after any real undo, including keys reported `~ kept`. This is documented ("a key that stayed is the user's now") and tested, so it is intended.
- `packages/runtime/src/setup/scope.ts:87`: the symlink check is a check-then-write gap, and it covers only `.claude` and the settings file. This is partial hardening and matches the stated requirement.
- Rejected: `permissions.deny` is recorded only when setup added the whole list (`json-file.ts` `place` marks a differing list `kept`), so a user's pre-existing deny entries are never recorded or removed.
- Rejected: the "unrecorded" `~` line for a pre-existing default key is the specified and tested behavior (`setup-scope.test.ts`, "a value setup did not record adding it is kept with ~").
- `version-control.md:10`: the "never work on the platform-assigned branch" rule matches the requirement. Refusal handling (stop, report, ask) is present.
- Instruction coherence: `assignments.md:11` ("repair as new local commits") against "each commit atomic and passes the gates alone" is reconciled by squash-merge by default, so it is non-blocking. Merge-forward after a squash is covered in both `stack-plan.md:6` and `version-control.md:18`.
